function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool
function.description: Writes the provided content to a Markdown (.md) file on the disk. This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the most common tools and platforms you can use to book flights—whether you’re looking for a simple web interface, a mobile app, or an API for developers:

| Category | Tool / Platform | What it offers |
|----------|-----------------|----------------|
| **Online Travel Agencies (OTAs)** | **Expedia** | One‑stop shop for flights, hotels, car rentals, and packages. |
| | **Kayak** | Aggregates prices from many airlines and OTAs; includes price alerts. |
| | **Skyscanner** | Great for flexible dates and “cheapest month” searches. |
| | **Google Flights** | Fast, intuitive interface; shows price trends and alternative airports. |
| | **Momondo** | Similar to Skyscanner but often finds slightly cheaper fares. |
| | **Priceline** | Known for “Name Your Own Price” and Express Deals. |
| | **Orbitz** | Loyalty program (Orbucks) and bundle discounts. |
| | **Travelocity** | Similar to Orbitz; often runs promotions. |
| | **Hotwire** | Focuses on last‑minute deals and “opaque” bookings. |
| | **CheapOair** | Good for discounted fares and promo codes. |
| | **Booking.com** | Primarily hotels, but also offers flight bookings. |
| | **Trip.com** | Strong presence in Asia; offers multi‑city itineraries. |
| | **Airfarewatchdog** | Alerts for flash sales and deep discounts. |
| | **Hipmunk** | Visual “fuzzy” search; shows flight duration vs. price. |
| | **Travelzoo** | Curated deals and coupons for flights. |
| | **Lastminute.com** | Great for spontaneous trips. |
| | **Opodo** | European OTA with competitive fares. |
| | **eDreams** | Focus on low‑cost carriers. |
| | **TUI** | Combines flights with holiday packages. |
| | **JetRadar** | Aggregates low‑cost carriers worldwide. |
| | **FlightNetwork** | Offers “price match” guarantees. |
| | **CheapTickets** | Discounted fares and promo codes. |
| | **TravelSupermarket** | UK‑based price comparison. |
| | **Travelpayouts** | Affiliate network; offers flight search widgets. |
| | **Airfarewatchdog** | Alerts for flash sales and deep discounts. |

**Developer‑friendly APIs**

| API | What it offers |
|-----|----------------|
| **Skyscanner API** | Search flights, hotels, car rentals; price alerts. |
| **Google Flights API (via Google Cloud)** | Flight search, price history, and itinerary building. |
| **Kiwi.com API** | Multi‑city itineraries, hidden‑city pricing, and fare alerts. |
| **Amadeus Self‑Service APIs** | Flights, hotels, car rentals, and travel commerce. |
| **Travelport Universal API** | Comprehensive travel booking across airlines, hotels, and car rentals. |
| **Sabre APIs** | Global distribution system (GDS) for airline inventory and booking. |
| **FlightAware API** | Real‑time flight status and historical data. |
| **OpenSky Network API** | Real‑time flight tracking data. |
| **Airline‑specific APIs** (e.g., Delta, United, Southwest) | Direct booking and fare data for those carriers. |

**Mobile Apps & Widgets**

| App / Widget | Highlights |
|--------------|------------|
| **Hopper** | Predicts best booking times; price alerts. |
| **Momondo** | Visual price comparison; flexible date search. |
| **TripIt** | Organizes itineraries; integrates with flight bookings. |
| **Airbnb Experiences** | Book flights + local experiences. |
| **Google Trips** | (Legacy) integrates flight, hotel, and activity planning. |
| **FlightRadar24** | Real‑time flight tracking; can help confirm bookings. |

**Corporate & Loyalty Programs**

| Program | What it offers |
|---------|----------------|
| **Miles & More** | Earn miles on partner airlines; redeem for flights. |
| **SkyMiles (Delta)** | Earn and redeem miles; elite status benefits. |
| **AAdvantage (American Airlines)** | Earn miles; upgrade options. |
| **Executive Club (British Airways)** | Earn Avios; upgrade and lounge access. |
| **Flying Blue (Air France/KLM)** | Earn miles; partner airline network. |

**Specialty & Niche Platforms**

| Platform | Focus |
|----------|-------|
| **Airfarewatchdog** | Alerts for flash sales. |
| **Secret Flying** | Publishes error fares and deep discounts. |
| **Scott's Cheap Flights** | Email alerts for cheap fares. |
| **The Flight Deal** | Deals on business class and premium cabins. |
| **LowFareFinder** | Low‑cost carrier deals. |
| **CheapTickets** | Promo codes and last‑minute deals. |
| **Travelzoo** | Curated travel deals. |
| **JetRadar** | Low‑cost carrier search. |
| **FlightNetwork** | Price match guarantee. |

---

### Quick Tips for Booking

1. **Compare Across Multiple OTAs** – Prices can vary by a few dollars; use a price‑comparison site or browser extensions (e.g., Skyscanner, Kayak).
2. **Check the Airline’s Own Site** – Some airlines offer exclusive fares or lower fees when booking directly.
3. **Use Flexible Dates** – Most OTAs let you view a calendar of prices; flying mid‑week is usually cheaper.
4. **Set Price Alerts** – Tools like Hopper, Skyscanner, and Google Flights will notify you when fares drop.
5. **Consider Nearby Airports** – A short drive to a different airport can save money.
6. **Book Early for Business/First Class** – Premium cabins often have better availability and lower prices when booked well in advance.
7. **Look for Error Fares** – Sites like Secret Flying publish rare, deeply discounted tickets.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like deeper dives into any specific platform, API integration details, or how to set up automated price alerts!
